front_blocks.md: Describe the three steps of enzyme action.

back_blocks.md: **1.** Enzymes and substrates move about **randomly** in solution.
**2.** An enzyme and its **complementary substrate collide**, an **enzyme-substrate complex** forms, and the reaction occurs.
**3.** The **products** form and are released from the active site. The enzyme is **unchanged** and goes on to catalyse further reactions.

front_blocks.md: Outline the method for this investigation.

back_blocks.md: Add 5 cm<sup>3</sup> **starch solution** to a test tube and bring it to the chosen temperature.
Put a drop of **iodine solution** in each well of a spotting tile.
Add 2 cm<sup>3</sup> **amylase**, mix, and start the timer.
Every minute, transfer a droplet of the mixture to the next well of iodine.
Stop when the iodine **no longer changes colour**, and record the time. Repeat at least twice more, then repeat across a range of temperatures.

front_blocks.md: How does a pH that is too high or too low affect an enzyme?

back_blocks.md: The **bonds** holding the amino acid chain together are **disrupted or destroyed**.
This **changes the shape of the active site**, so the **substrate can no longer fit**, and the rate of activity falls.
